name: Daria Khlebnikova
about_artist_p1: Daria Khlebnikova was born in Omsk and graduated from the Faculty of Arts at OmGPU. She works both on her own artistic projects and in illustration for games, books, and other projects.
exhibition_2023: 2023 – Solo exhibition "Elusive Dreams", Kvadrat Gallery, Omsk
exhibition_2024: 2024 – 5th Regional Exhibition of Young Artists, Union of Artists, Omsk
exhibition_2025: 2025 - Interdisciplinary exhibition of contemporary art "NextArt. Immersion", CCA Artetage Vladivostok
about_art_p1: I create worlds that weave themselves into rhythmic structures, inviting the viewer to journey inward, into a space of living, breathing infinity, and aim to evoke a sense of encountering something supernatural, at once familiar and strange. Paintings emerge like puzzles, assembled layer by layer, from everything I love. My work is influenced by artistic and literary movements such as dark fantasy, surrealism, magical realism, cosmism, romanticism, and symbolism. Often, imagery is rooted in archetypal and religious motifs. Dreams are a big source of inspiration, I’ve been collecting and recording them for years.
metamorphosis_description: An ongoing series I have been working on since 2022, exploring contrasts and transformations — of people, creatures, deities, forms, styles, and emotions.
intergalactic: Intergalactic Ensemble of Crystal Gnomes on the Toad Planet
intergalactic_description: When I listen to music, it often generates visual images in my mind, mostly forms, lines and patterns rather than color. This work was influenced by the cosmic jazz of Coltrane, Sun Ra, and medieval music. Molecules grow from tiny points, becoming increasingly complex until, at a certain moment, they gain consciousness and begin to play their cosmic music, creating this space, a paradise garden in a world where there is no boundary between humans and nature, where abstractions transform into living beings and scenes flow seamlessly into one another. The Planet of Toads is not so far from here, somewhere in the Andromeda Galaxy.
embrace_description: In this painting, I aimed to create a space that feels primordial and ancient, like the dreamtime and even more ancient reptilian and amphibian epochs, long before the emergence of humans and language. It is not so much a specific myth as the raw material from which myths arise, a place beyond time, evoking states that we may not consciously remember, but carry within us as a memory of existing in the world before the separation of humans from nature.
prince_amigdala_description: This painting emerged from a dream in which a black creature descended upon me, tearing apart the familiar fabric of reality. It was tangible to me, yet invisible to another character in the dream. The figure of the “Prince” embodies the boundary between neurophysiology and mythology. The amygdala is associated with memory, fear, and emotional responses. It is an archetypal image of a being that brings change to the existing reality. The architecture in the background is an organic temple, a kind of four-dimensional space composed of psychic reflections. Each fragment contains a trace of another fragment, each image becomes an entry point into the next. The shards become material for new, yet unknown worlds. This is how the process of inner transformation and rewriting of certain outdated parts of ourselves looks to me.
night_description: This work weaves together references to Dante’s Divine Comedy, the Tibetan Book of the Dead, and mythologies from various cultures to construct an inner landscape where the soul’s  journey unfolds. Bardo Chönyid is a transitional state filled with archetypal visions. Whether peaceful or terrifying, they are ultimately illusory: manifestations of the mind itself, intended to guide the soul toward enlightenment. On the left side of the composition, we see spiritual guides — Virgil, Charon, the Minotaur — over whom miniature muses hover. From the chaos emerge various beings, dakinis and harpies. In the lower right corner, a labyrinth of neurons represents the mind as the source of all these illusions. Simple, tiny figures grow and transform into deities — a metaphor for both the evolution of ideas within consciousness and the evolution of the physical world shaped by sentient beings. All of it arises within the mind that generates reality. Skulls and female forms symbolize the unity of life and death, while serpents represent the flow of vital energy. As one travels deeper into the painting, the forms become increasingly abstract, leading the viewer beyond the familiar, toward the white light of the Dharmakaya, the non-dual state of pure awareness.
snake_and_flower_main_description: 2022 38х54cm tempera, watercolor, isograph, pencil on paper
snake_and_flower_description:
Part of me, in the moment, is fully immersed in the experience, while another part exists outside of time, present in all moments at once, containing every state while being more than their sum. Perhaps this part of the soul remains untouched, a place where nothing ever truly happens.
…In this dream, I was in my room, only it had been turned upside down. I looked out through the door. Instead of the hallway, there was an enormous space, a vertical tunnel. Neither its upper nor lower end was visible, and even the opposite wall could barely be made out in the distant darkness. It seemed that the walls were covered with doors and arches.
And there was a gigantic red serpent. Serpentine heads grew from its body, their mouths opened, and entire clusters of new heads emerged from them, and from their mouths came others, and so on and so on. In the dream, I had the thought that the serpent might symbolize time, while the heads represented all possible variations of every event. And so it twisted in coils and flew from one end of infinity to the other.
Then it noticed me. I ran back toward the window and hid in the wardrobe. I was afraid that the heads would crawl into the room, begin multiplying uncontrollably, and fill the entire space. But the heads only peered into the room, pressed their eyes against the doorway, and watched me…
phenomena_description: A series of my early works created between 2013 and 2019 at different times, united by the theme of human encounters with various phenomena and visions both in the world and within oneself.
spirtis_description: A series of works I began in 2023, dedicated to fantastic semi-abstract beings.
road_description: This work is about spiritual transformation, and bringing order to chaos. The central image is the angel of the desert and the sword that cuts through the mental defilements. The landscape resembles the desert of reality, overflowing with meaningless information. I worked with stone textures in a way that they live their own life, unfolding as organic forms. The overloaded mass of the landscape merges into a single chthonic environment.
meeting_description: The experience of stepping beyond the boundaries of the self and meeting phenomena greater than human existence — whether destiny, chaos, love, or the forces of nature. These are moments of contact with the Other, and at the same time of recognizing reflections of oneself, often ambivalent in their nature.
river_description: An allegory of a person’s inner struggle with themselves and the conflicting forces within the soul. The armor symbolizes the ego’s defensive psychological mechanisms, masks, and aggressive drives toward control and domination over nature. The river represents purification, movement, and transformation.
labyrinth_description: The infinities of nature and the mind, unfolding in opposite directions of vision, outward into the world and inward into the self, through two modes of seeing. It is also about states of entanglement and wandering, as well as moments of crystalline clarity.
